query: How does incident resolution efficiency vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a finer semantic categorisation of incidents derived from short_description, giving a new axis to group resolution efficiency beyond the coarse original 'category'. Values are sound readings of the source text. Slightly overlaps with the existing category column but is more granular.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Asset-type dimension is a genuine new grouping axis for efficiency analysis and largely well grounded (printer, monitor, network_device match descriptions). Mapping 'database' to software_application is a defensible inference; NULLs for silent rows are acceptable.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom taxonomy adds a useful axis for correlating failure modes with resolution time. Extractions like connectivity_failure are well warranted, but 'malfunction_general' (310 rows) is a large catch-all that risks near-constant behaviour and some symptoms are inferred from terse text ('not working properly' -> malfunction_general is reasonable).

per_column.name: self_resolved_by_assignee
per_column.rationale: The short_description text gives no basis for whether the assignee self-resolved; this is not derivable from the provided source fields. The 'True' for a connectivity incident with only a description is an unsupported assertion. Marginal usefulness and weak grounding.

per_column.name: software_trigger_present
per_column.rationale: A binary flag that is heavily skewed (446 false) and somewhat generic. Where descriptions mention software it is derivable, but for most terse hardware descriptions the false default is a reasonable 'not stated' behaviour. Limited analytical leverage for this efficiency query.

per_column.name: requires_replacement
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (486 false / 14 true), reducing analytical leverage. Values are rarely stated in short descriptions, so 'false' is often an assumption rather than a grounded reading, though it aligns with a plausible 'not stated' default. Weak but not clearly contradicted.

judge.rationale: The categorical columns (incident_category, affected_asset_type, failure_symptom_type) give genuine new grouping axes that directly support analysing resolution efficiency across category-like dimensions and are mostly well grounded in the short_description text. The three boolean flags are weaker: self_resolved_by_assignee is not derivable from the provided text and appears fabricated on at least one sample, while software_trigger_present and requires_replacement are highly skewed/near-constant with values that are often assumed rather than grounded. Scored on the two necessary conditions only, without penalising for any missing columns.
